mainKeyword: best through the wall air conditioners
metaDescription: Six through-the-wall air conditioners compared on sleeve fit, EER, 115V supply, heat options and room coverage, with sleeve and installation notes for 2026.
expertTake: The LG 10,000 BTU wall unit is the best pick because it states an EER of 10.7, covers 440 square feet and runs on 115V from a brand with deep service coverage. The Keystone 8,000 BTU with supplemental heat is the value pick for a room that needs both functions. If you only have a window and no wall sleeve, skip this category, because these units cannot simply be set in a sash.
introParagraphs: A through-the-wall air conditioner lives in a framed opening in an exterior wall, held in a metal sleeve, rather than sitting in a window. That frees the glass, seals better against drafts and hides the unit in the building, which is why apartments and additions use them.

The catch is the sleeve. The wall opening has to match the chassis, the supply has to match the plug and the unit must be built for wall use, not just a window. Check all three before you pick a model.

products.name: LG 10,000 BTU Through-the-Wall AC, 115V, EER 10.7
products.description:
LG's wall unit lists 9,800 BTU of cooling, an EER of 10.7 and R-32 refrigerant, with coverage up to 440 square feet on a 115V supply. EER is cooling output divided by power at fixed conditions, so a 10.7 is a respectable figure for a wall unit of this size.

The listing is clear that it is suited to a through-the-wall installation and is not made for a window, which matters because a sleeve unit has a different chassis. Against the 11,800 BTU LG it covers 90 fewer square feet but is easier on the electrical supply, and against the OLMO units it has a stated EER and a larger service network.

Ownership is the wall-unit routine: a washable filter, a coil clean in spring and checking the sleeve seal each year. The sleeve is a separate purchase, so confirm the size before ordering. If you are replacing an older unit, take the old chassis dimensions and the sleeve depth to the store or compare them against the listing, because a few inches of difference decides whether it fits.
products.bestFor: A bedroom or living room up to 440 square feet with an existing wall sleeve.
cons: Not suitable for a standard window

products.name: LG 11,800 BTU Through-the-Wall AC, 115V, EER 10.6
products.description:
The larger LG lists 11,800 BTU, EER 10.6 and coverage up to 530 square feet on a 115V supply with R-32 refrigerant. It is built for through-the-wall installation and is not recommended for a window.

The difference from the 10,000 BTU model is capacity and a one-tenth EER drop, which is normal as the compressor grows. It suits a large bedroom or a small open living area. Against the OLMO 12,000 BTU it has a stated EER and a stronger brand, but the OLMO adds a smart kit.

As with all of these, the sleeve is a separate item, the opening must match the chassis and a dedicated 115V circuit is wise because current at this size is high. Clean the filter every few weeks and the coil each spring. Because it is heavy, plan for two people and a temporary support so the unit does not drop onto the sleeve edge during installation.
products.bestFor: A large bedroom or open area up to 530 square feet.
cons: Needs a dedicated circuit at this current

products.name: OLMO 12,000 BTU 115V Through-the-Wall AC, Built-In Smart Kit
products.description:
OLMO's 12,000 BTU wall unit is cooling only, runs on 115V single phase at 60Hz, uses R-32 refrigerant and has a built-in smart kit for app control. The listing asks you to verify that you have the right receptacle, which is a real warning at this size.

It does not state an EER in the data, so efficiency is a gap compared with the LG units. It does offer the highest cooling capacity here on a standard supply, and the smart kit adds scheduling. The wall sleeve is not part of the listing, so budget for one.

Ownership is the usual wall-unit routine. Check the receptacle before you buy, keep the filter clean and inspect the sleeve seal each year, because a leaky sleeve wastes much of the cooling. The built-in smart kit is convenient for scheduling, but keep the manual controls reachable so you can run the unit if the app is unavailable.
products.bestFor: A large room where the most 115V capacity and app control are wanted.
cons: No EER stated in the data
Sleeve and receptacle must be checked

products.name: OLMO 8,000 BTU 115V Through-the-Wall AC and Heater, with Wall Sleeve
products.description:
This OLMO combines 8,000 BTU of cooling with a heating function, a built-in smart kit and a remote, on a 115V single-phase supply. The listing title names a wall sleeve, which makes it one of the few options here that can be installed without a separate sleeve purchase.

Including the sleeve removes a common point of confusion, since sleeve size has to match the chassis. The data does not give a heating capacity or an EER, so treat the heat as supplemental. Against the TCL and Keystone it offers the sleeve bundle, and against the LG it has less capacity.

Ownership is routine. Seal the sleeve to the wall, keep the filter clean and check the supply receptacle, since the listing explicitly warns to verify it. Because the bundle includes a sleeve, check that its depth matches the thickness of your wall before you start cutting.
products.bestFor: A room of about 350 square feet that needs cooling, some heat and a complete install kit.
pros: Sleeve is part of the listing
Cooling and heating in one unit
cons: No heating capacity or EER in the data
Smaller capacity than the 11,800 BTU LG

products.name: TCL 8,000 BTU Smart Through-the-Wall AC with 4,200 BTU Heater
products.description:
TCL pairs 8,000 BTU of cooling with a 4,200 BTU heater, a built-in dehumidifier mode and Wi-Fi control on a 115V supply. The stated 4,200 BTU of heat is the useful number: it is about 1,230 watts of resistance heat, a little under a standard space heater, so it takes the chill off a room, not warms a cold one.

Its role is the smart, mid-capacity wall unit. Compared with the Keystone, which lists the same 4,200 BTU of heat, it adds Wi-Fi and voice, and compared with the OLMO heat unit it states its heating capacity.

Ownership is routine. The sleeve is separate, so check the opening size before you order, and keep the filter and coil clean. Use the dehumidifier mode in shoulder seasons when the air is damp but the temperature is mild, which saves running the full cooling cycle.
products.bestFor: A bedroom of about 350 square feet that wants app control and some heat.
cons: Wall sleeve is a separate item
Smaller capacity than the LG units

products.name: Keystone 8,000 BTU Wall AC with 4,200 BTU Supplemental Heat
products.description:
Keystone's wall unit lists 8,000 BTU of cooling and 4,200 BTU of supplemental heat, with dehumidification and fan modes on a 115V supply. It is the plain version of the combo wall unit, without the app features of the TCL.

That simplicity is the value. It cools and heats an average bedroom, uses a standard circuit and has fewer electronics to fail. Compared with the TCL it gives up Wi-Fi, and compared with the LG it has less capacity and no stated EER.

Ownership is the wall-unit routine: a sleeve is required, the filter needs regular washing and the sleeve seal needs a yearly check. Confirm the sleeve opening before you order. Because it has few electronics, it is a reasonable choice for a rental or a seldom-used guest room where simplicity beats features.
products.bestFor: A bedroom of about 350 square feet that needs cooling and light heat at a lower price tier.
pros: Cooling plus 4,200 BTU of supplemental heat
cons: No EER stated in the data
Wall sleeve is a separate item

buyingCriteria.explanation: A through-the-wall unit slides into a metal sleeve set in the wall, and the chassis must match the sleeve dimensions. The LG listings state that these units are not made for window installation, and the OLMO 8,000 BTU heat unit lists a sleeve with it. Measure your existing opening before choosing a model. If the old sleeve is rusted or sagging, replace it at the same time, because a new unit in a bad sleeve will leak.

The LG 10,000 BTU states an EER of 10.7 and the LG 11,800 BTU states 10.6. EER is cooling output divided by power draw at fixed conditions. Units without a stated figure, such as the OLMO and Keystone, leave you to guess, so favor a stated EER when running cost matters.

All six here run on 115V, but at 11,800 or 12,000 BTU the current is high enough to need a dedicated circuit. The OLMO listing warns to verify the receptacle, and that is good advice for every unit. A wrong plug type turns an easy install into an electrician visit. If the circuit is shared with lights or outlets, an 11,800 or 12,000 BTU unit can trip the breaker on the hottest afternoons.

The TCL and Keystone each list 4,200 BTU of heat, about 1,230 watts, while the OLMO 8,000 BTU heat unit gives no figure. That output takes the chill off a bedroom but does not heat a cold room. Treat it as supplemental.

A wall sleeve that leaks air wastes more cooling than a poor EER. Caulk the outside, insulate the gap and use the unit's gasket. Many owners find a sleeve leak is the cause of a unit that never catches up. A line of foam tape between the sleeve and the framing also quiets rattles and blocks drafts.

The LG 10,000 BTU covers up to 440 square feet and the 11,800 BTU unit up to 530, which is about 22 BTU per square foot. The 8,000 BTU units suit about 350 square feet. Oversizing makes a room cold and clammy, so match the room.

howWeEvaluated.title: Wall-unit suitability
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked that each unit was built for a wall sleeve and noted which listings include one. The LG units are explicit about not being window units, and the OLMO 8,000 BTU heat unit names a sleeve.

howWeEvaluated.title: Efficiency evidence
howWeEvaluated.description: We gave credit to stated EER figures, 10.7 on the LG 10,000 BTU and 10.6 on the LG 11,800 BTU, and discounted units that give none.

howWeEvaluated.title: Electrical fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted the supply requirements and the risk of a wrong receptacle. All six use 115V, but the larger units need a dedicated circuit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heat and features
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the 4,200 BTU heaters on the TCL and Keystone with the unstated figure on the OLMO. Stated numbers scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Support
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered brand service networks based on owner feedback patterns. LG scored highest, TCL and Keystone were in the middle and OLMO lost points for newness.

howToChoose.subheading: For Replacing an Old Sleeve Unit Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A chassis that matches the existing sleeve, the same electrical receptacle and a similar capacity. Measure the sleeve opening, depth and any front trim before ordering.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The LG units are the safest swap for an older through-the-wall unit, and the OLMO 8,000 BTU heat unit is the easiest if you have no sleeve at all.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The room is large or you want a stated efficiency. The LG 10,000 BTU or LG 11,800 BTU repays that spend with EER and service.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The room is an average bedroom. The Keystone 8,000 BTU does cooling and heat for less.

maintenance.why: A clogged filter cuts airflow and freezes the coil. Dry it fully before refitting. Wall units sit in a fixed spot, so a monthly habit is easy to keep.
A leaking sleeve loses cooling and lets in insects. Re-caulk the outside and replace the gasket.
Dust films the coils and cuts efficiency. A soft brush and a fin comb restore airflow.
A warm plug signals a poor connection at high load. Replace damaged outlets.
Wall units drain through the base pan. A blocked drain causes drips on the wall.

faq.q: Can I put a through-the-wall unit in a window?
faq.a: Not safely. The LG listings state that these are not made for window installation, because the chassis and weight distribution differ from a window unit. Use a unit designed for a sash instead.

Yes. The sleeve holds the unit and seals it to the wall. The OLMO 8,000 BTU heat listing includes one, and the others require a separate purchase sized to the chassis. The sleeve size must match the chassis, so check dimensions in the listing carefully.

For a wall unit around 10 to 11 is typical, and the LG units state 10.7 and 10.6. Higher EER means lower running cost, but it matters most if you run the unit for months. A stated EER lets you estimate running cost, which is worth the effort for a unit that runs all summer.

Some can. The TCL and Keystone list 4,200 BTU of heat, which is supplemental. It will take the chill off a bedroom but not heat a cold one. A separate space heater is more effective when real warmth is the goal.
Check the receptacle before you buy, and remember that sleeve wiring is often older than the unit going into it. Verify the receptacle and plug type before you order.

faq.q: How long do wall units last?
faq.a: Often ten years or more with regular filter and coil cleaning, since they are not carried in and out each season. A leaking sleeve is the usual cause of early trouble. Keeping the outside louvers clear of leaves and nests also protects the condenser from overheating.
